additions.title: The Life He Protected

journalBlocks.text: The warrior remembered a doorway beside the eastern wall. Someone had marked a child's height upon its frame; the newest line still lay below the latch. On patrol he used to notice another mark appearing, then another. It was a measure no report of the kingdom included.
He did not defend the stone because he believed it eternal. He defended the mornings in which someone could grow taller. The wall was only what stood around them.

additions.title: A Warning Remembered

journalBlocks.text: At the gate, the warrior watched people begin answering the traveler's questions with the answers they hoped to hear. A warning that proved useful once became a reason to neglect the next uncertainty. He remembered a guard turning away an ordinary report because it had not appeared among the stranger's predictions.
The warrior kept that report. Nothing disastrous followed that day. That was why the habit was so easy to dismiss.
Trust had begun to decide which warnings were allowed to count.

additions.title: A Place That Remembered

journalBlocks.text: At one sanctuary door, the warrior stopped before the step he usually took with his shield raised. The opening had already begun. He waited, lowered the shield, and approached differently. For a moment the room offered space for a movement he had not made.
What watched him had remembered a habit. The mismatch did not prove the sanctuary harmless, or blind to what came next. It showed him something smaller: its recognition could be mistaken.

additions.title: The Unfinished Promise

journalBlocks.text: The memory of the breaking contains a movement the warrior could not explain afterward. Before his hand reached for the collapsing barrier, it closed as though around the handle of a cup. The gesture was useless there. It belonged to another place, to a quieter exchange whose words would not return.
He had remembered the pressure of making an agreement before he remembered what the agreement asked of him. I cannot recover its words from the grief that followed.
He knew he had promised something. He could not yet tell obligation from grief.

additions.title: What He Carried Forward

journalBlocks.text: On the broken roads, the warrior packed the weakest travelers' provisions where they could reach them. He left his own beneath the rest. When asked why, he could give no account of learning the arrangement.

The fourth companion had once repacked their supplies that way after a long argument about distance. The warrior had mocked the extra trouble, then copied it. A useful kindness survived the name of the person who taught it. He carried that forward without knowing whose example it was.

additions.title: The Repeating Memory

journalBlocks.text: In one returning battle, the warrior remembered where the first blow would fall. He also remembered stepping toward it. This time he noticed someone behind his shoulder before he moved. He placed his shield differently.

The danger felt familiar; the person he protected did not. He could not tell whether this was another hour, another path, or a memory borrowing the shape of both. He recorded the difference instead of discarding it.
Recognition gave him a moment to consider. It did not tell him what he owed that moment.

additions.title: The First Calculation

journalBlocks.text: Beside the first calculation, the scholar had left an interval instead of a single answer. It allowed for choices he had not observed: a delayed departure, a changed intention, someone deciding against the road before them. Later he copied the neat result and left the interval behind.

The discarded marks had been part of his understanding, not a blemish upon it. He recovered them before he attempted the calculation again. The page now keeps the uncertainty beside the answer it qualifies.

additions.title: The Unexplained Signature

journalBlocks.text: The fourth signature occupied an unusual place in the old diagram. The other marks sat beside the paths being traced. This one stood beside an empty comparison space. A narrow return stroke joined it to the place where an observation could be entered after the work was done.
The missing participant had not merely supplied another strand. He had been assigned to check what the diagram claimed against what someone actually experienced.
Removing that signature had also removed a place from which the plan could be questioned.

additions.title: The Memory Threads

journalBlocks.text: One notation in the sanctuary gave a remembered person a single mark. Beside it, the scholar had listed several things that made recognition possible: a name, a habitual movement, an argument left unfinished. When the name faded from one recollection, the movement remained.

He had treated the mark as though it measured one indivisible thing. This example showed otherwise. The connection could not be understood by counting names alone. He retained the separate observations instead of forcing them back into the neat symbol.

additions.title: An Incomplete Answer

journalBlocks.text: There was an unfinished calculation on the reverse of the plan. The scholar had described an opening through the connected memories, then left the final condition empty. It was not a missing quantity. It asked whether the people carried through that opening would understand what was being taken from them.
He could estimate a change in the pattern. The empty condition concerned people who would have to live with that change.
He could calculate an opening. He could not calculate consent on another person's behalf.

additions.title: The Hour That Returned

journalBlocks.text: A familiar chime returned while the scholar was comparing his notes. The sound was the same. The cup beside him was warmer than his earlier mark recorded, and a fold in the page lay the other way. He could not establish whether the hour had repeated or two paths had approached the same event.
For once he preserved the disagreement. He wrote down the warmth, the fold, and the uncertain order. A recurring sign was no longer enough to erase everything that differed around it.

additions.title: The Persistent Thread

journalBlocks.text: The scholar tried to locate the enduring connection upon several maps of the broken paths. Its position shifted with the map. The relationships he could trace from it remained recognizable. He had been searching for a fixed place when the evidence described something held between histories.
He stopped copying its apparent position as though that were its identity. Beside each study he recorded which recollections still led toward it, and which had fallen silent.
The useful question was becoming what the anchor connected, rather than where he could draw it.

additions.title: A Forgotten Life

journalBlocks.text: A discarded impression preserved a sleeve repaired with two uneven stitches. The hand wearing it kept adjusting the cuff before reaching toward someone beyond the fragment. The Reaper could recover neither a face nor the occasion. He could see that someone had taken time to mend what another person would wear.
The account of the lost futures had counted their disappearance. He added this smaller evidence of living: a repair made badly, patiently, and for someone else. The wound was not the whole record.

additions.title: The Fourth Shadow

journalBlocks.text: Before the fourth shadow crossed the threshold, it waited. The Reaper had paused to examine a trace behind the others. The shadow held its place until he turned toward the passage, then moved with him. The recovered motion was so ordinary that it had almost escaped the account.
An imitation might have followed the three shapes ahead. This delay concerned the person who had fallen behind. The fourth presence had made room for someone whose attention was elsewhere.
What he recovered was more than a missing count. Someone had noticed him waiting.

additions.title: The Promise Without Witnesses

journalBlocks.text: After promising to remember, the fourth companion followed the others' departing steps with his hand against the stone. Three different rhythms passed beneath his fingers. The Reaper remembered him repeating them once after the footsteps themselves had faded.

He had tried to keep more than a list of names. He was attending to the ways the others moved when no explanation was needed. The attempt makes the promise more human. It offers no proof that a human memory could withstand what followed.

additions.title: The Two Wills

journalBlocks.text: In a recovered instant of the breaking, the same reaching gesture seemed to end in two intentions. One movement opened a way for someone to depart. The other closed around what it could still hold. The Reaper could not separate their shapes, but neither could he make their purposes agree.

The contrast remained inside the damaged recollection. Whatever had bound the wills together had not turned every impulse into consent. He recorded the disagreement without pretending it offered a way to undo the fusion.
Sharing an existence had not made their wishes the same.

additions.title: An Ending Interrupted

journalBlocks.text: Beneath the vanished ending, the Reaper noticed the pressure left by its strokes. The ink had ceased to form the intended conclusion, but the paper still carried the attempt. He followed the shallow marks without trying to complete them.

A refusal could stop the account from closing. It could not make the attempt to close it innocent. I had pressed those strokes into the paper. I will not conceal that beneath another certainty, or fill the other voice's silence with what I think it means.

additions.title: The Last Remaining Echo

journalBlocks.text: Within the merged impression, the Reaper recognized an old habit. Where the face would not resolve, a movement still left room beside it, as the fourth shadow had waited at the threshold. It was slight enough to be dismissed as damage in the recollection.

He kept it. The surviving pattern included a way of attending to someone else. Recovering that detail did not separate the wills or restore the friend they had known. It changed what the Reaper would listen for.
There was still a relation to acknowledge before there was an answer about how to free him.
